ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Oxygen in a normoxemic patient

A patient with confirmed acute coronary syndrome is comfortable at rest with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. He has no respiratory distress. Which statement best describes routine supplemental oxygen in this situation?

  1. It replaces antiplatelet therapy
  2. It dissolves coronary thrombi directly
  3. It should never be used even if saturation falls below 90%
  4. It is not routinely recommended solely because ACS is present
  5. It is mandatory at maximum flow for every ACS patient
Answer and explanation

It is not routinely recommended solely because ACS is present

Routine oxygen has no established benefit in normoxemic ACS; hypoxemia creates an indication.

Option explanations

It is not routinely recommended solely because ACS is present: Routine oxygen has no established benefit in normoxemic ACS; hypoxemia creates an indication.

It is mandatory at maximum flow for every ACS patient: Routine high-flow oxygen is not recommended for normoxemia.

It replaces antiplatelet therapy: Oxygen does not replace antithrombotic treatment.

It dissolves coronary thrombi directly: Oxygen is not a fibrinolytic agent.

It should never be used even if saturation falls below 90%: Hypoxemia is an indication for supplemental oxygen.
